name: Okra Soup
summary: A quick, lightly slimy soup of chopped okra, palm oil, crayfish and fish or meat that begs for a swallow.
story: Okra soup is an everyday dish in many Nigerian homes and is made in several regional styles, from thick and slimy to a more brothy version. It is eaten with swallows such as eba, amala or fufu. It cooks quickly, so it is a popular weeknight choice.

items.name: Fresh okra
items.note: washed, then chopped small or grated

items.name: Meat or fish
items.note: cooked beef, shaki or fresh fish

steps.title: Prepare okra
steps.text: Trim the okra and chop it finely or grate it. Smaller pieces release more slime, so size controls texture.

steps.title: Start the base
steps.text: Heat the palm oil gently for 1 to 2 minutes, then add the onion and cook until soft. Stir in the pepper and crayfish for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add stock and proteins
steps.text: Pour in the stock and add the cooked meat and smoked fish. Bring to a gentle simmer for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add the okra
steps.text: Stir in the okra, a stock cube and a little salt. Cook uncovered for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring, until the okra is tender yet bright green and the soup thickens.

steps.title: Add leaves
steps.text: Fold in the greens if using and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, just until wilted and bright.

steps.title: Taste and serve
steps.text: Taste and adjust the salt and pepper. The soup should be thick enough to cling to a spoon and stretch slightly; serve hot.

tips: Do not overcook the okra or it turns grey and loses its flavour.
Leave the lid off while the okra cooks to keep it green.
A pinch of baking soda is sometimes used for extra draw, but a small pinch only.

swaps.swap: Frozen chopped okra works; add it straight from frozen.
Use vegetable oil if you cannot find palm oil; the soup will be paler and less fragrant.
Smoked mackerel or smoked trout adds a similar savoury note.
